The problem

Online revenue is not a listing problem. It is a commercial system.

Twelve variables decide aggregator performance — menu, pricing, discounts, ads, conversion, availability and more. Most restaurants optimise them separately. Foresight manages them as one connected system.

Framework

Five disciplines. One connected system.

Discovery → Conversion → Economics → Repeat → Scale

01

Discovery

Get found: search relevance, placement, catalogue, reach.

02

Conversion

Turn traffic into orders: menu architecture, combos, cart-to-order.

03

Economics

Know what each order earns: pricing, discounts, contribution.

04

Repeat

Keep the demand you paid for: ratings, availability, repeat rate.

05

Scale

Reproduce it at the next outlet or city.

Chennai · Swiggy · Oct 2025–Mar 2026

Trupthi Veg Restaurant

₹3.74 lakh → ₹25 lakh in monthly revenue.

Scorecard — verified

Monthly revenue
₹3.74L → ₹25L 6.7×
CPC ROAS
361% → 961%
Discounted share of orders
48.86% → 23.60%
Repeat customers
55% → 69%
Menu score
0 → 93/100
Preparation time
12.35 → 7.24 min

The situation

Nearly half of all orders carried a discount. The catalogue scored 0/100. Ads returned ₹3.61 per rupee. The storefront was competing on price, not relevance.

The work

Catalogue rebuilt against menu-score criteria. Blanket discounting replaced with targeted combos and thresholds. Campaigns rebuilt around converting items. Preparation-time programme run with the kitchen.

Revenue rose 6.7× while discounting fell by half — the growth was not bought. Repeat customers at 69% means a growing share of volume arrives with no acquisition cost.

Evidence: Swiggy partner dashboard exports, Oct 2025–Mar 2026.

Baga–Calangute, Goa · Swiggy · Nov 2025–Jan 2026

Trails of Taste

₹4.64 lakh → ₹8.46 lakh peak monthly GMV.

Scorecard — verified

Peak monthly GMV
₹4.64L → ₹8.46L +82%
Monthly orders
535 → 877 +64%
Subzone market share
12.55% → 18.25%
Combo score
11 → 100/100

The situation

Peak season entered with a combo score of 11/100 and 12.55% subzone share. In a seasonal market, share not taken inside the window is gone.

The work

Combo architecture rebuilt from 11 to 100. Campaigns restructured for the season, weighted to peak weeks. Demand-capture mechanisms deployed.

GMV rose faster than orders — a fifth of the gain came from larger baskets, which carry no extra delivery or acquisition cost.

₹8.46L is the December peak; ₹7.43L the January comparison month.
Evidence: Swiggy partner dashboard exports, Nov 2025–Jan 2026.

OMR–Perungudi, Chennai · Swiggy & Zomato · Oct 2025–Jan 2026

Coromandel Tiffin

₹4.23 lakh → ₹7.20 lakh in combined monthly revenue.

Scorecard — verified

Combined monthly revenue
₹4.23L → ₹7.20L
Zomato orders
785 → 1,604
Zomato sales
₹2.23L → ₹4.83L
Cart-to-order conversion
35.2% → 43.0%
Availability
79% → 95.6%
Swiggy menu score
0 → 93.6/100

The situation

Availability at 79% — the storefront was effectively closed one day in five. The Swiggy catalogue scored 0/100 and only 35.2% of carts became orders.

The work

Availability protocol established first. Catalogue rebuilt. Cart friction cleared. Advertising weighted to Zomato, the higher-headroom platform.

The first 16.6 points of availability recovery are revenue the business was already entitled to — the cheapest revenue in any engagement, and the reason the sequence started there.

Evidence: Swiggy and Zomato partner dashboard exports, Oct 2025–Jan 2026.

Bengaluru · Zomato · July 2026 (launch, month one)

Tia The Baker

₹2.71 lakh in net sales in the first month.

Scorecard — verified

Net sales
₹2,70,774 after platform deductions
Delivered orders
778
Average order value
₹348

The situation

A launch — no ranking history, no ratings, no repeat base. Month one had to be won on relevance and catalogue quality alone.

The work

Complete storefront build. Search-focused menu architecture, naming and descriptions. Catalogue structured for occasion and basket. Opening price architecture set for the market.

An AOV of ₹348 in a dessert category means catalogue structure, not discounting, carried the value.

This is net sales, not GMV — not comparable to the growth results above.
Evidence: Zomato partner dashboard, July 2026.

Platform Growth Audit

Request a Platform Growth Audit.

The audit establishes where your online revenue is actually constrained — visibility, conversion, economics, retention or operations — and the sequence to clear it. It is an application, not an enquiry form.

What happens next

A senior member of the practice reviews every application. If it is a fit, we return with an initial read on your listings and a proposed scope. If not, we say so and explain why.

What we do not do

No instant calendar, no published price list. Scope follows the diagnosis.

Before you apply

Have your Swiggy and Zomato listing links to hand. The initial read is done against the live storefronts, not a description of them.

Submitted details are used only to assess fit and prepare the initial read. See Privacy.
